vpd: Remove heavy library shflags The vpd_get_value was intended to be pretty fast with minimal dependency. `shflags` is too heavy and should be avoided. The argument '--create_cache=false' is now replaced by VPD_NEVER_CREATE_CACHE=1 When running "time vpd_get_value serial_number": Before (with shflags): real 0m0.037s user 0m0.022s sys 0m0.020s After (use environment variable): real 0m0.007s user 0m0.004s sys 0m0.005s BRANCH=None BUG=chromium:970145 TEST=emerge-$BOARD vpd; vpd_get_value serial_number Cq-Depend: chromium:1642714 Change-Id: I6da52fa655010070350cad9bf056375aa15e3979 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1642771 Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org>

init: usermode-helper: fix argc check While I added code to handle the argv0 difference between direct user invocation & kernel invocation, I forgot to adjust the argc check. For programs that take no args, we're currently triggering crashes we shouldn't. For example, when the kernel runs poweroff, it's with argv=["/sbin/poweroff"] which trips this check. BUG=chromium:915974 TEST=running by hand still works Change-Id: I26f68c0c52bf208bf2d46b28bdcdaf9592565b79 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1635934 Commit-Ready: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Allen Webb <allenwebb@google.com>

libbrillo: Add CRLF after last boundary marker For multipart HTTP messages, the last encapsulation boundary marker still needs a CRLF after the second -- (https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc1341/7_2_Multipart.html). This is causing our crash servers to mark our crash uploads as "malformed true". BUG=chromium:968831 TEST=Uploaded crash report. Confirmed that "malformed true" was not appearing. Change-Id: Ib5e8364d4fd770b75b793fce320791656bd2cad2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1638948 Commit-Ready: Ian Barkley-Yeung <iby@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ian Barkley-Yeung <iby@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>

This would catch some misuse of Error/Fatal/Log v.s. Errorf/Fatalf/Logf. CRAS: audio_thread - Ignore next_cb_ts of draining streams In the current version, when a stream is draining and there are some samples in a share memory, we will wake up at the next_cb_ts of that stream. However, if a device is full, we can not take out all samples from the stream. Meanwile, the next_cb_ts is not updated because the stream is draining. It causes the audio thread always wake up at that next_cb_ts and trigger busy loop. To fix this problem, we can ignore next_cb_ts if the streams is draining. The first reason is we don't need to fetch that stream any more. The second reason is a device already have its own wake up time, which is the time that a device needs more samples. So we don't need to worry about that these samples will not be played. (see cras_iodev_frames_to_play_in_sleep) BUG=chromium:958492 TEST=Do not trigger busyloop when device buffer is full. (Tested on eve by seting incorrect rate in cras.) FROMGIT: ASoC: soc-core: fixup references at soc_cleanup_card_resources() commit 53e947a0e1f7 ("ASoC: soc-core: merge card resources cleanup method") merged cleanup method of snd_soc_instantiate_card() and soc_cleanup_card_resources(). We need to set NULL to it. 2nd is card->dapm and card create debugfs, but its dentry is still exist even though it was removed. We need to set NULL to it. FROMGIT: Revert "ASoC: core: use component driver name as component name" Using component driver as a name is not unique and it breaks audio in certain configurations, e.g. Hardkernel Odroid XU3 board where following components are registered: - "3830000.i2s" with driver name "snd_dmaengine_pcm" - "3830000.i2s-sec" with driver name "snd_dmaengine_pcm" - "3830000.i2s" with driver name "samsung-i2s" This reverts commit b19671d6caf1ac393681864d5d85dda9fa99a448.
